svg.title: FastPIFU Cardiology — Skill Structure & Workflow
svg.desc: Flowchart showing file structure, three-tier condition classification, two-layer decision process, workflow steps, and output verdicts for the fastpifu-cardiology skill.
svg.text: Last updated 2 July 2026 · Self-contained · No internet required
(5 NHS/GIRFT docx re-verified & dated 2026-07-02; SOP template unchanged)
① YAML description — always in context
② SKILL.md body — loaded on trigger
Read all 5 .docx files (PIFU guidance + GIRFT). Fallback: nhs-pifu-criteria-summary.md if any .docx unreadable.
Extract and internally note: inclusion criteria · exclusion criteria · monitoring caveats — for each condition.
Read the prn02169 SOP template. Three condition tiers, applied alongside the universal Layer 2 checklist:
Arrhythmia, valve disease, HF: explicit NHS inclusion
Clear match → binary verdict, high confidence.
sourced rule) — NOT a non-pathway condition.
Applies to ALL patients regardless of condition.
· no secondary care monitoring · patient activation
· no device safety concern. Fail any one → ❌
All 6 clearly met → PIFU; any fail → ❌
GIRFT-informed tier (chest pain/angina/post-MI): uses 2d GIRFT rules + Layer 2 (2a) directly — NOT the 2b bar.
Careful consideration (not exclusion): safeguarding · contact difficulty · frailty · low literacy · 3+ comorbidities.
Accepted formats: PDF · Word (.docx) · plain text · pasted. Read all documents before reaching a verdict.
⬛ FIRST QUESTION: can this patient be DISCHARGED entirely? (GIRFT discharge-first principle)
Check Discharge-to-GP table (Step 2d) before concluding PIFU-eligible. "No further follow-up" → 🔄 Discharge.
Identify: sub-specialty · subtype · diagnosis · medications (dose + recency) · devices (remote monitoring?) · procedures
Flag data gaps: NYHA · LVEF · serial echo · anticoag stability · eGFR trend · frailty · admission date · antiarrhythmic class
Common traps: biochem vs symptoms · rate of echo change · co-medication monitoring · subtherapeutic dose · deferred plan
Apply: NHS-pathway (1+2d) for arrhythmia/valve/HF/cardiomyopathy · GIRFT-informed (2d+2a) for chest pain/angina/post-MI
· SOP+POTS (2b+2c) for POTS · SOP only (2b), elevated bar, for any other condition with no guidance at all
Patient · Condition · Document type · Pathway type · Data gaps · Eligibility factors · Criteria source
· Verdict · Reasoning · Suggested PIFU timescale (condition-specific — never a flat default)
· Always cite criteria source; disclose missing pathway
· Exclusion flag ≠ auto NOT_ELIGIBLE — check mitigating factors
· If doubt: BORDERLINE > NOT_ELIGIBLE; BORDERLINE > ELIGIBLE
· Two-layer decision process (Layer 1 NHS + Layer 2 SOP)
· What to do when no guideline exists at all (4-step protocol)
active decompensation · end-of-life/palliative · pending investigations · patient unwilling · new monitored medication
Fully self-contained — no internet access required or used · NHS/GIRFT sources re-verified 2 July 2026
Arrhythmia: PAF · Permanent AF · Persistent AF · SVT · VT · Pre-excitation (WPW) · Ventricular ectopy · Atrial flutter · Other Arrhythmias
Valve disease: AS · AR · MR · MS · MVP · BAV · Post-TAVI/TEER/repair Heart failure: HFrEF · HFpEF · HFmrEF
Cardiomyopathy (ischaemic/non-ischaemic) & inherited channelopathy — arrhythmia-sourced rule, not PIFU by default
GIRFT-informed (Step 2d, not a full NHS pathway):
POTS · any other condition with no NHS/GIRFT guidance
